Have Got to and Going to Have to for What Is Necessary
You can use have got to or be going to have to when expressing necessity either in present or future ideas.
You can use have to or have got to in order to show necessity in present ideas, however have got to is more informal and used in spoken English.
You have (got) to have an efficient communication when transmitting the design to others.
In interrogative sentences you use have to with the auxiliary do/does , but with have got to , you placesend the auxiliary have/has at the beginning of the sentence.
Have you got to change the architecture? – No, I don't have to!
Do you have to change the architecture? – No, I don't have to!
Notice you use have to rather than have got to in negative statements.
You can use the auxiliary be going to or will to express the idea of necessity in the future.

images.text: Now you've decided to build software and specialized apps for your business, you have got to know that there are some basic and important principles that you will need to bear in mind to succeed in the process of creating a good and stable architecture. Such principles are going to ease your life and the process of constructing the architecture, but when we say principles, we have got to talk about two main groups, architecture and design principles. The first one is related to the architecture itself and the second one will help you minimize costs and requirements while maximizing the architecture.

We can say that among the many ways of maximizing performance, we have chosen some that will help you boost your architecture, like, firstly, take into account when you are building an architecture you will need to build it to change instead of last, that means you are going to have to build the architecture to suffer changes, so that it addresses new requirements. That, on the other hand, means you are going to have to use an iterative approach to add details and ensure the architecture will be perfectly optimized.

One of the main question that arise when talking about architectural design is how you are going to maximize the usability and extendibility of the architecture. Well, that is not a cakewalk, but not unbearable either. Firstly, you are going to have to separate the concerns, that is, to divide components into specific features. You may want to group the components into logical layers to understand the structures of the system in an organized way, another way to maximize your architecture is by restricting knowledge with the principle of least knowledge, this way, you avoid objects having key information of other components inside them.
